items.title: Protect vulnerable road users
items.simple: People walking, biking, skating or in wheelchairs can get badly hurt. It is against the law to drive in a distracted or careless way around them. Drive so you can avoid other people's mistakes.
items.official: Drivers also share the road with vulnerable road users including pedestrians and those on bicycles, wheel chairs, skateboards, roller skates, scooters, animals and animal-drawn vehicles. It is illegal to drive distracted and carelessly around vulnerable road users. It is your responsibility to adjust your driving to avoid others' mistakes and assure everyone's safety. Pedestrians are especially prone to serious injury when struck. Be careful around schools, playgrounds and in residential areas where people may be playing or crossing the street.

items.title: Turning? Pedestrians go first
items.simple: When you turn right or left, people walking have the right-of-way. Wait until they have crossed the street all the way. Then make your turn.
items.official: Be especially aware of pedestrians when making a right or left turn. They have the right-of-way. Allow pedestrians to completely cross the street before beginning your turn.

items.title: Never pass at a crosswalk
items.simple: Do not pass another car at a crosswalk. It is against the law. The other car may hide a person walking in front of it.
items.official: Passing at a crosswalk is illegal. You may not see pedestrians crossing the road in front of other vehicles.

items.title: Stay stopped for pedestrians
items.simple: Watch for people crossing the road. Stop and stay stopped until they have passed your lane. Do not creep forward while they are in front of you.
items.official: Be alert for pedestrians crossing the road. Stop and remain stopped until pedestrians have passed the lane in which your vehicle is stopped.

items.title: Cane or guide dog: full stop
items.simple: A cane or guide dog means the person may be blind or may not see well. You must come to a full stop for that person. Older people and people with disabilities may move slowly.
items.official: Drivers are required to come to a full stop for a pedestrian using a cane or guide dog, as this indicates blindness or vision impairment. Remember that the elderly and people with disabilities may move slowly.

items.title: Not stopping: Class 1 misdemeanor
items.simple: You must come to a full stop for people who are crossing the road legally. If you fail to stop and you badly hurt or kill someone, it can be a Class 1 misdemeanor.
items.official: Drivers are required to come to a full stop for pedestrians who are lawfully crossing a roadway. Failing to stop and causing serious bodily damage or death can result in a Class 1 misdemeanor.
items.mnemonic: Walkers come first. Not stopping and hurting someone: Class 1.

items.title: Bicycles: same right-of-way
items.simple: A bike rider on the road has the same right-of-way as a car. Bike riders must follow many of the same laws as drivers. Some bike riders may not know or obey the rules. Slow down when you approach them.
items.official: Bicyclists on a roadway generally has the same right-of-way as the driver of a motor vehicle. Bicyclists are subject to many of the same laws as drivers, however, some may not know or obey the rules. Slow down when you approach bicyclists.

items.title: Bikes may use center of lane
items.simple: Bike riders may ride in the middle of the lane when needed. They may do this when they are about to turn left. They may also do it when the lane is too narrow to share with a car.
items.official: Bicyclists are allowed to ride in the center of the lane, when necessary, such as when they are about to turn left or when the lane is too narrow to share side-by-side with a car.

items.title: Bikes: not on interstates
items.simple: Bike riders may use all public roads except interstates and most freeways. Watch for bikes going either way on sidewalks, shared-use paths and two-way bike lanes.
items.official: Bicyclists are legally allowed on all public roads except interstates and most freeways (limited access highways). Drivers should be aware of bicyclists riding in either direction on sidewalks, shared-use paths, or two-way separated bike lanes.

items.title: Never pass in a bike lane
items.simple: Never drive in a marked bike lane to pass someone. Keep your car in your own lane. You may enter a bike lane only when you need to turn left or right.
items.official: Using marked bicycle lanes is prohibited by motor vehicles, including while passing. (Section 2: Drivers should not drive in the bicycle lane except when necessary to turn left or right.)

items.title: Pass bikes by 3+ feet
items.simple: Pass a bike rider with at least 3 feet of space. If the lane is too narrow for 3 feet, change lanes to pass. Give bikes plenty of room and be ready to stop suddenly.
items.official: State law requires motorists to pass cyclists with at least three feet of clearance. If the lane is not wide enough to allow for a three-foot clearance, the motorist must change lanes to pass safely. Give bicyclists plenty of room when passing and be prepared to stop suddenly.

items.title: Check for bikes and motorcycles
items.simple: Bikes and motorcycles are small, so they slip into your blind spot easily. Look for them before you pull out, change lanes or turn. Also look for them before you back up, open your door or cross an intersection.
items.official: A bicycle's small size allows it to slip into your blind spot easily. Always check for bicyclists before you pull out, change lanes, turn, back up, open the door, or proceed through an intersection. A motorcycle's size allows it to slip into your blind spot easily. Always check for motorcycles before you pull out, change lanes, turn, back up or proceed through an intersection.

items.title: Look twice for motorcycles
items.simple: More than half of deadly motorcycle crashes involve cars. Often the driver did not see the motorcycle until it was too late. Look twice for motorcycles. Check twice before you pull out in front of one.
items.official: More than half of all fatal motorcycle crashes involve automobiles. Many crashes are caused by the motorist's failure to see a motorcycle in traffic. Look twice for motorcyclists. In more than half of all crashes involving motorcycles and automobiles, the other driver didn't see the motorcycle until it was too late. Drivers are conditioned to look for four-wheeled vehicles; but they don't expect to see two-wheeled vehicles. The size of a motorcycle can cause you to misjudge the motorcycle's speed and distance. Before pulling out into traffic, check twice for motorcycles and use extra caution before you pull out in front of one.

items.title: Motorcycle: add 1 second
items.simple: Never tailgate a motorcycle. Use the normal rule for following distance, then add one more second. In bad weather, double that distance.
items.official: Never tailgate a motorcycle (or any other vehicle). Allow yourself plenty of braking distance by adding an extra second to the following distance rule. In inclement weather, double this distance.
items.mnemonic: Motorcycle: plus 1 second. Bad weather: times 2.

items.title: Never share a motorcycle's lane
items.simple: A motorcycle rider uses the whole lane. Small bumps or trash on the road can make the rider move suddenly. Never drive beside a motorcycle in the same lane.
items.official: Although a motorcycle is not as wide as the lane, the rider will use the entire lane as traffic situations and road conditions change. A slight change or debris on the road surface can be a major obstacle for a motorcyclist. Expect the motorcycle to make sudden moves within the lane. Never drive beside a motorcycle in the same lane.

items.title: The Tide: Norfolk light rail
items.simple: Norfolk has a light rail system called The Tide. Its trains share the road with cars and bikes. Never drive around lowered gates. Expect a train on any track at any time.
items.official: There is a light rail train system in Norfolk called The Tide. Light rail trains share the road with motor vehicles and bicyclists, and they intersect with motor vehicle traffic at 27 locations along the 7.4 mile route. Pay attention to changing traffic patterns and always follow the roadway. Never drive around lowered crossing gates. Always look both ways before turning across train tracks. Expect trains on any track at any time. Always obey signs and traffic signals.

items.title: Never stop on train tracks
items.simple: Never stop, pass or shift gears on train tracks. Cross only when there is room to get all the way over. You must clear the tracks without stopping.
items.official: Never stop, pass or shift on train tracks. Don't cross train tracks unless you have enough room to cross without stopping and can clear the tracks to a safe distance.
items.mnemonic: Clear it all, or don't start at all.

items.title: Low speed vehicles: 21-25 MPH
items.simple: A low speed vehicle has four wheels and runs on electric or gas power. Its top speed is 21 to 25 MPH.
items.official: These electrically- or gas-powered four-wheel vehicles have a maximum speed ranging from 21 to 25 MPH.

items.title: LSVs: roads 35 MPH or less
items.simple: Low speed vehicles may use roads with speed limits of 35 MPH or less. The driver needs a license. A permit holder may drive one if a licensed driver rides along.
items.official: Low speed vehicles may be operated on public roads with speed limits of 35 MPH or less by licensed drivers or learner's permit holders accompanied by a licensed driver. Low speed vehicles must comply with all federal safety standards and must meet Virginia's requirements for passenger vehicle registration and insurance coverage.

items.title: Golf carts are not LSVs
items.simple: A golf cart is not a low speed vehicle. Don't mix them up. Low speed vehicles have four wheels. Their top speed is 21 to 25 MPH.
items.official: Golf carts are not classified as low speed vehicles.

items.title: Truck No-Zones
items.simple: Trucks, buses and RVs have danger areas around them called No-Zones. These areas are on the sides, in front and behind the vehicle. The driver may not see you there. Stay out of No-Zones.
items.official: Trucks, tractor-trailers, buses and recreational vehicles (RVs) are longer, higher and wider than other vehicles. They accelerate slowly and require greater stopping and turning distances. Plus, there are danger areas around these vehicles where crashes are more likely to occur. These areas are called No-Zones. No-Zones on the side, front and rear also include blind spots where your car disappears from the driver's view.

items.title: Mirror rule: see the driver's face
items.simple: Trucks have big blind spots on both sides. Look at the truck's side mirror. If you cannot see the driver's face in it, the driver cannot see you.
items.official: Trucks, tractor-trailers, buses and RVs have big No-Zones on both sides that are dangerous because these vehicles must make wide turns. These No-Zones or blind spots are much larger than your car's blind spots. If you can't see the driver's face in his side view mirror, then he can't see you.
items.mnemonic: See his face, or leave that place.

items.title: Rear No-Zone: don't tailgate trucks
items.simple: A truck driver cannot see your car right behind the truck. You cannot see the traffic ahead of the truck. If the truck stops suddenly, you have nowhere to go. Keep a safe following distance.
items.official: Trucks, tractor-trailers, buses and RVs have huge No-Zones directly behind them. The driver can't see your car behind his vehicle and you can't see what's happening in traffic ahead of his vehicle. If the truck, bus or RV brakes or stops suddenly, you have no place to go and could crash into the vehicle's rear-end. Always maintain a safe following distance.

items.title: Passing a truck: see its front
items.simple: After you pass a truck, do not cut in too soon. Wait until you see the whole front of the truck in your rearview mirror. Then pull in and keep your speed.
items.official: You could get rear-ended by a truck, bus or RV if you cut in front too soon after passing the vehicle or if you cut in front and then suddenly slow down. When passing, look for the entire front of the truck in your rearview mirror before pulling in front. And then, maintain your speed.
items.mnemonic: Whole truck front in the mirror? Now pull in.

items.title: Trucks need twice the stopping room
items.simple: Trucks, buses and RVs are slow to stop. They need nearly twice the time and room that a car needs. If you cut in front of a truck and slow down, it may not stop in time.
items.official: These vehicles need nearly twice the time and room to stop as cars.

items.title: Truck length and passing room
items.simple: A truck and its trailer can be up to 65 feet long. Passing one can take more than half a mile of clear road. Be sure you have the room before you pass.
items.official: A truck and its trailer may be as long as 65 feet and it may take you more than half a mile of clear road to pass.
items.mnemonic: 65 feet long, half a mile to pass.

items.title: Trucks swing wide to turn
items.simple: Big trucks, buses and RVs may swing wide to the left or right to turn. They can't see cars right behind or beside them. Never squeeze between a truck and the curb or another car.
items.official: Trucks, buses and RVs sometimes need to swing wide to the left or right to safely make a turn. They can't see the cars directly behind or beside them. Never try to squeeze between a truck, bus or RV and the curb or another vehicle.

items.title: Blind spots: 20 front, 200 back
items.simple: A truck's blind spots can reach up to 20 feet in front of the cab. Behind the truck, they can reach about 200 feet. Stay out of these blind spots.
items.official: In fact, their blind spots may stretch up to 20 feet in front of the cab and approximately 200 feet behind the vehicle.
items.mnemonic: 20 in front, 200 behind. Add a zero for the back.

items.title: Towing: twice as long
items.simple: Towing a trailer puts extra stress on your vehicle. It takes your vehicle twice as long to pass, stop, speed up and turn. Large side mirrors help you see better. Remember the No-Zones.
items.official: These trailers are attached to mid-sized cars and trucks with safety chains and a trailer hitch. Large side mirrors are generally needed to increase visibility. Towing a trailer places additional stress on the vehicle; it takes the vehicle twice as long to pass, stop, accelerate and turn.

items.title: Trailer safety check every trip
items.simple: Check your trailer before every trip. Make sure the hitch pin, coupler and safety chains are secure. Check the plug and all the lights. Before you tow on public roads, practice in an empty parking lot.
items.official: Before driving a vehicle with a light to medium trailer attached, perform a safety inspection before each trip. Ensure: the pin securing the ball mount to the receiver is intact; the hitch coupler is secured; safety chains are properly attached; the electrical plug is properly installed; brake lights, turn signals, and license plate lights are functioning properly. Before pulling a trailer on public roads, find a location such as a vacant parking lot to practice.

items.title: Trailer sways? Slow down
items.simple: If your trailer starts to sway, slow down. Your trailer makes your vehicle longer. Allow for that extra length when you change lanes.
items.official: When driving a vehicle with a light to medium trailer attached: always allow for the added length of the trailer when you change lanes; if your trailer starts to sway, slow down.

items.title: Backing a trailer: hand at bottom
items.simple: To back up a trailer, put your hand on the bottom of the steering wheel. Move the wheel left to send the trailer left. Move it right to send it right. If you cannot see, have someone guide you.
items.official: When backing up, place your hand on the bottom of the steering wheel. If you cannot see where you are backing up, have someone outside to help guide you. To back the trailer to the left, use your left hand to move the wheel left. To back the trailer to the right, use your right hand to move the wheel to the right.
items.mnemonic: Hand at the bottom: the trailer goes where your hand goes.

questions.prompt: Who is responsible for adjusting their driving to avoid other people's mistakes?
questions.explain: It is your responsibility as a driver to adjust your driving to avoid other people's mistakes and keep everyone safe.

questions.prompt: What must you do when you turn right or left and a pedestrian is crossing?
choices: Turn quickly before the pedestrian reaches you
Let the pedestrian completely cross the street before you turn
Honk so the pedestrian moves faster
questions.explain: Pedestrians have the right-of-way when you turn, so let them completely cross first.

questions.prompt: When you are turning, what is true about pedestrians who are crossing the street?
choices: They must yield to turning cars
They have the right-of-way only at night
questions.explain: Pedestrians have the right-of-way when you turn, so be especially aware of them.

questions.prompt: The light is green and you want to turn right. A pedestrian is crossing. What must you do?
choices: Wait until the pedestrian has completely crossed
Turn because the light is green
questions.explain: When you turn, let pedestrians completely cross the street before you begin your turn.

questions.prompt: What does the law say about passing another vehicle at a crosswalk?
choices: It is legal if you signal first
It is legal if no pedestrians are in view
It is legal on one-way streets
questions.explain: Passing at a crosswalk is illegal, because you may not see pedestrians crossing in front of the other vehicle.

questions.prompt: Why should you never pass a vehicle that is stopped at a crosswalk?
choices: The other driver may get angry
You may not see a pedestrian crossing in front of that vehicle
You must always stay in the left lane
questions.explain: Another vehicle can block your view of pedestrians who are crossing in front of it.

questions.prompt: What must you do when a pedestrian is crossing in front of your stopped vehicle?
choices: Stay stopped until the pedestrian has passed your lane
Honk to hurry the pedestrian along
Go when the pedestrian is halfway across your lane
questions.explain: You must stop and stay stopped until the pedestrian has passed the lane your vehicle is in.

questions.prompt: You stopped for a pedestrian. When may you move again?
choices: When the pedestrian steps off the curb
When the car behind you honks
When the pedestrian looks at you
When the pedestrian has passed the lane you are stopped in
questions.explain: You must stay stopped until the pedestrian has passed your lane.

questions.prompt: This sign warns of a pedestrian crossing. What must you do if a person is crossing in front of you?
choices: Slow down and pass behind the person
Stop and stay stopped until the person passes your lane
Go around the person on the left
questions.explain: You must stop and stay stopped until the person has passed the lane you are stopped in.

questions.prompt: What must you do when you see a pedestrian using a cane or a guide dog?
questions.explain: Drivers must come to a full stop for a pedestrian who is using a cane or a guide dog.

questions.prompt: What is most likely true about a pedestrian who is using a cane or a guide dog?
choices: The person is a police officer
The person is blind or has a vision impairment
The person is a school crossing guard
questions.explain: A cane or a guide dog most likely means the person is blind or has a vision impairment.

questions.prompt: Which pedestrians may move slowly when crossing the street?
choices: Older people and people with disabilities
questions.explain: Older people and people with disabilities may move slowly when they cross.

questions.prompt: A pedestrian is lawfully crossing the road. You fail to stop and cause serious injury or death. What can happen to you?
questions.explain: If you fail to stop and cause serious injury or death, the result can be a Class 1 misdemeanor.

questions.prompt: For which pedestrians are drivers required to come to a full stop?
choices: Pedestrians who are standing at a bus stop
Pedestrians who are lawfully crossing the roadway
Pedestrians who are walking on the sidewalk
Pedestrians who are waiting in a parking lot
questions.explain: You must come to a full stop for pedestrians who are lawfully crossing a roadway.

questions.prompt: What right-of-way does a bicyclist riding on the roadway generally have?
choices: The right-of-way only in bike lanes
The same right-of-way as a motor vehicle driver
questions.explain: Bicyclists on a roadway generally have the same right-of-way as drivers of motor vehicles.

questions.prompt: What should you do when you approach a bicyclist?
choices: Honk so the bicyclist moves over
questions.explain: Slow down when you approach bicyclists, because some may not know or obey the rules.

questions.prompt: This sign warns of bicycles. Which of these does a bicyclist on the road generally have?
choices: No right to use the road
The same right-of-way as a car
questions.explain: Bicyclists on the road generally have the same right-of-way as drivers of motor vehicles.

questions.prompt: When may a bicyclist ride in the center of the lane?
choices: When the bicyclist is riding on an interstate
When the lane is too narrow to share side by side with a car
When the bicyclist wants to race cars
Never, because bicyclists must always ride on the shoulder
questions.explain: Bicyclists may ride in the center of the lane when necessary, such as when the lane is too narrow to share.

questions.prompt: You see this marking. A bicyclist ahead is riding in the middle of your narrow lane. What does the law say about that?
choices: It is allowed when the lane is too narrow to share with a car
It is illegal, and the bicyclist must move to the curb
It is allowed only at night
It is allowed only on interstates
questions.explain: Bicyclists may ride in the center of the lane when it is too narrow to share side by side with a car.

questions.prompt: A bicyclist moves to the center of the lane just before an intersection. What is probably true about the rider?
choices: The rider is breaking the law
The rider is about to stop and park
The rider is trying to block you
The rider is about to turn left
questions.explain: Bicyclists may ride in the center of the lane when they are about to turn left.

questions.prompt: Which public roads are bicyclists NOT legally allowed to use?
questions.explain: Bicyclists may use all public roads except interstates and most freeways.

questions.prompt: Which statement is true about bicyclists on sidewalks, shared-use paths and two-way separated bike lanes?
choices: They ride only in the same direction as traffic
They may ride in either direction
They are never there, because bicycles must stay on the road
questions.explain: Drivers should watch for bicyclists riding in either direction on sidewalks, shared-use paths and two-way bike lanes.

questions.prompt: What does the law say about driving a motor vehicle in this marked lane to pass another car?
choices: It is allowed if no bicycles are in the lane
It is allowed if you use your turn signal
It is allowed during rush hour
questions.explain: Motor vehicles may not use marked bicycle lanes, including while passing.

questions.prompt: Which is true about marked bicycle lanes?
choices: Cars may not use them, even to pass
Cars may use them to pass slow traffic
Cars may park in them for short stops
Cars may use them when they are empty
questions.explain: Motor vehicles are not allowed to use marked bicycle lanes, including while passing.

questions.prompt: What is the least amount of clearance Virginia law requires when you pass a bicyclist?
questions.explain: State law requires you to leave at least 3 feet of clearance when you pass a bicyclist.

questions.prompt: What must you do if a lane is too narrow to pass a bicyclist with 3 feet of clearance?
choices: Pass anyway at a slow speed
Use the bike lane to pass
Honk so the bicyclist moves onto the shoulder
questions.explain: If the lane is not wide enough for 3 feet of clearance, you must change lanes to pass the bicyclist.

questions.prompt: You see this sign and a bicyclist ahead. What is the least space you must leave when you pass the bicyclist?
questions.explain: The law says to pass a bicyclist with at least 3 feet of space.

questions.prompt: When should you check for bicyclists?
choices: Before you pull out or change lanes
Before you turn or back up
Before you open your car door
questions.explain: Always check for bicyclists before you pull out, change lanes, turn, back up, open your door or go through an intersection.

questions.prompt: Why are bicycles and motorcycles easy to miss?
choices: They always ride on the sidewalk
Their small size lets them slip into your blind spot
They are only on the road at night
questions.explain: The small size of a bicycle or motorcycle lets it slip into your blind spot easily.

questions.prompt: A motorcycle can easily hide in the area shown. What should you do before you change lanes?
choices: Speed up and change lanes quickly
Check your blind spot by glancing over your shoulder
questions.explain: A motorcycle can slip into your blind spot, so look over your shoulder before you change lanes.

questions.prompt: What do more than half of all fatal motorcycle crashes involve?
questions.explain: More than half of all fatal motorcycle crashes involve automobiles.

questions.prompt: What was true of the car driver in more than half of crashes between motorcycles and cars?
choices: The driver was speeding on an interstate
The driver was driving in fog
The driver did not see the motorcycle until it was too late
The driver was following too far behind
questions.explain: In more than half of these crashes, the car driver did not see the motorcycle until it was too late.

questions.prompt: Before you pull out into traffic, what should you do about motorcycles?
choices: Do not check, because they will yield to you
Check only in the right lane
questions.explain: Check twice for motorcycles and use extra caution before you pull out in front of one.

questions.prompt: What about a motorcycle can make you misjudge its speed and distance?
questions.explain: The small size of a motorcycle can make you misjudge its speed and distance.

questions.prompt: What should you do when you follow a motorcycle?
choices: Follow closer so the rider can see you
Follow closer because motorcycles stop slowly
Flash your lights so the rider moves over
Add an extra second to the following distance rule

questions.prompt: What should you do when you follow a motorcycle in bad weather?
choices: Cut your following distance in half

questions.prompt: Which statement is true about sharing a lane with a motorcycle?
choices: You may drive beside a motorcycle because it is narrow
You may share the lane if you signal
You should never drive beside a motorcycle in the same lane
You may share the lane on highways
questions.explain: Never drive beside a motorcycle in the same lane. The rider may use the whole lane.

questions.prompt: Why might a motorcycle make sudden moves within its lane?
choices: Because the rider is showing off
Because of debris or small changes in the road surface
Because the rider wants to let cars share the lane
questions.explain: Debris or a slight change in the road surface can be a big obstacle for a motorcyclist.

questions.prompt: The gates are down at this light rail crossing. What must you do?
choices: Stop and do not drive around the lowered gates
Drive around the gates if no train is in sight
questions.explain: You must never drive around lowered crossing gates.

questions.prompt: In which city does the light rail train system called The Tide run?

questions.prompt: What should you do when you drive near light rail tracks?

Expect trains only on the left track
Assume the train will stop for you
Expect trains on any track at any time
questions.explain: Expect a train on any track at any time.

questions.prompt: Which of these should you never do when you cross light rail or train tracks?
choices: Stop, pass or shift gears on the tracks
Cross when you have room to clear the tracks
questions.explain: Never stop, pass or shift gears on train tracks.

questions.prompt: What must be true before you start across train tracks?
choices: The car ahead is already on the tracks
You have room to cross without stopping and can clear the tracks
questions.explain: Do not cross train tracks unless you have enough room to cross without stopping and can clear the tracks.

questions.prompt: Traffic ahead is stopped just past this crossing. What should you do?
choices: Wait back from the tracks until there is room to clear them
Stop on the tracks behind the last car
Pass the stopped cars on the tracks
questions.explain: Never stop on train tracks. Cross only when you have room to clear them.

questions.prompt: What is the maximum speed of a low speed vehicle?
questions.explain: A low speed vehicle has a maximum speed of 21 to 25 MPH.

questions.prompt: Low speed vehicles may be driven on public roads with which speed limits?

They are the same as golf carts

The requirements for commercial truck licensing
No requirements, because they are exempt

Golf carts are allowed on all public roads
Golf carts are classified as motorcycles
Golf carts are not classified as low speed vehicles

questions.prompt: Which of these is NOT a low speed vehicle?
choices: A four-wheel electric vehicle with a top speed of 25 MPH
A four-wheel gas vehicle with a top speed of 21 MPH
A four-wheel electric vehicle with a top speed of 23 MPH

questions.prompt: What are the shaded areas around this truck called?
questions.explain: The danger areas around trucks, buses and RVs are called No-Zones. Crashes are more likely there.

questions.prompt: Which statement is true about trucks, buses and RVs compared to cars?
choices: They speed up faster and stop in less distance
They speed up slowly and need more distance to stop and turn
They can always see cars behind them
questions.explain: Trucks, buses and RVs speed up slowly. They also need more distance to stop and to turn.

questions.prompt: Which statement is true when you cannot see a truck driver's face in the truck's side mirror?
choices: You are at a safe distance
The truck driver can see you clearly
The truck driver cannot see you
You should stay there and honk
questions.explain: If you cannot see the driver's face in the truck's side mirror, the driver cannot see you.

questions.prompt: Which statement about the blind spots on the sides of trucks, buses and RVs is true?
choices: They are much larger than a car's blind spots
They are smaller than a car's blind spots
They are the same as a car's blind spots
They are only on the left side

questions.prompt: Why is it dangerous to follow a truck too closely?
choices: Trucks stop in less distance than cars
The truck driver can always see you in the mirror
The truck driver cannot see you, and you cannot see traffic ahead
questions.explain: Directly behind a truck, the driver cannot see you and you cannot see traffic ahead of the truck.

questions.prompt: Where do trucks, buses and RVs have a huge No-Zone?
choices: Nowhere, because they have large mirrors
questions.explain: Trucks, buses and RVs have huge No-Zones directly behind them.

questions.prompt: After you pass a truck, what should you do before you pull back in front of it?
choices: Wait until your back bumper passes its front bumper
Wait until the truck driver flashes his lights
Wait until you are one car length ahead
Wait until you can see the entire front of the truck in your rearview mirror
questions.explain: Look for the entire front of the truck in your rearview mirror before you pull in front of it.

questions.prompt: What should you do after you pass a truck and pull in front of it?
questions.explain: After you pull in front of a truck, maintain your speed.

questions.prompt: Which of these could get you rear-ended by a truck?
choices: Cutting in too soon after you pass it
Cutting in front of it and then suddenly slowing down
questions.explain: Cutting in too soon, or cutting in and then slowing down suddenly, can get you rear-ended by a truck.

questions.prompt: How much time and room do trucks, buses and RVs need to stop, compared to cars?

questions.prompt: Why is it dangerous to cut in front of a large truck and then slow down?
choices: The truck can stop faster than you
Trucks have smaller blind spots than cars
The truck needs nearly twice as much room to stop as a car does

questions.prompt: A truck and its trailer may be up to how many feet long?

questions.prompt: Passing a truck may take more than how much clear road?

questions.prompt: A truck ahead is swinging wide to make a right turn. What should you do?
choices: Pass the truck on the right
Stay back and never squeeze between the truck and the curb
Squeeze between the truck and the curb
Honk your horn and pass quickly

questions.prompt: Up to how far in front of the cab may a truck's blind spot stretch?

questions.prompt: Compared with driving without a trailer, how long does it take to pass, stop, speed up and turn while towing a light to medium trailer?

It takes three times as long

questions.prompt: How is a light to medium trailer attached to a vehicle?

questions.prompt: Which of these should you do before each trip with a trailer?
choices: Check that the safety chains are properly attached
Check that the hitch coupler is secured
Check that the brake lights and turn signals work
questions.explain: Before each trip, check the hitch pin, coupler, safety chains, electrical plug and lights. All of them are part of the safety check.

questions.prompt: What is a good thing to do before you pull a trailer on public roads?
choices: Practice in a place such as a vacant parking lot
questions.explain: Before you pull a trailer on public roads, find a place such as a vacant parking lot to practice.

questions.prompt: When should you do a trailer safety inspection?
questions.explain: You should do a trailer safety inspection before each trip.

questions.prompt: What should you do if the trailer you are towing starts to sway?
questions.explain: If your trailer starts to sway, slow down.

questions.prompt: What should you do when you change lanes while towing a trailer?
choices: Allow for the added length of the trailer
Do not use your turn signal
questions.explain: A trailer makes your vehicle longer, so always allow for its added length when you change lanes.

questions.prompt: Where should you place your hand when you back up with a trailer?
choices: On the top of the steering wheel
On the bottom of the steering wheel

choices: Use your left hand to move the wheel to the left
Use your right hand to move the wheel to the right
Turn the wheel hard to the left with both hands

questions.prompt: What should you do if you cannot see where you are backing up with a trailer?
choices: Sound your horn and keep backing
Have someone outside help guide you

questions.prompt: When you pass a bicyclist, you should give plenty of room. What else should you be prepared to do?

questions.explain: When you pass bicyclists, give them plenty of room and be ready to stop suddenly.

questions.prompt: Which of these vehicles have No-Zones where your car can disappear from the driver's view?

questions.prompt: What should you do when you drive near The Tide, the light rail train in Norfolk?
choices: Pay attention to changing traffic patterns and follow the roadway
Drive on the tracks to pass traffic
Ignore the signals when no train is near

questions.prompt: Why should you be especially careful near schools, playgrounds and residential areas?
choices: People may be playing or crossing the street
